transcript.text: Monopoly Profit, Loss & Shutdown
MICROECONOMICS
MICRO-39
Time: 5 minutes
Outcome: Calculate Monopoly Profit, Loss & Shutdown.
Difficulty: Intermediate
THE CORE IDEA

Monopoly profit or loss is measured after the profit-maximizing output and demand-based price have been found. The firm must cover avoidable variable cost. Output optimization and profit measurement are separate steps in monopoly analysis. Profit or loss equals (P−ATC)Q at the chosen output.
HOW TO RECOGNIZE IT
Choose monopoly output where rising marginal cost equals marginal revenue, then read price from demand.
At that output, compare price with average total cost to determine profit or loss.
Compare price with average variable cost to decide whether a loss-making monopolist operates in the short run.
Measure profit or loss as the price-cost gap multiplied by output.
WATCH OUT

A common mistake is to mix output choice with profit measurement. Output optimization and profit measurement are separate steps in monopoly analysis. Profit or loss equals (P−ATC)Q at the chosen output.
WORKED EXAMPLE: MONOPOLY PROFIT OR LOSS

Horizontal axis: quantity; vertical axis: price / cost. Demand D slopes downward from price 60 to zero at quantity 120; MR reaches zero at quantity 60. At quantity 36, MR and rising MC meet at 24, demand is at 42, and ATC is at 27. Dashed guides mark those values. Demand and MC intersect at quantity 60 and price 30. ATC is U-shaped with its minimum near quantity 48.
The firm chooses 36 units where MR equals MC. At that output, demand gives a price of $42 and ATC is $27. Profit per unit is $42 - $27 = $15, so total economic profit is $15 x 36 = $540.
CHECK YOURSELF
Why does P>MC not prove positive economic profit?
